Situation1: Your friend has misunderstood the tone of your text message and replied sounding hurt. You need to call them right now to explain.
Expectation2: Ensure client satisfaction and address any concerns or complaints professionally
Situation2: A first-time visitor looks disappointed with the colour tone in the mirror.
Story: My phone buzzed in my pocket just as I was finishing up the highlights on my new client. I glanced down and saw a message from Mia, my best friend. Her words stung: “I can’t believe you’d say that to me.” My heart dropped. She’d misunderstood my joke from earlier, and now she sounded genuinely hurt. I knew I needed to call her right away, to explain, to fix this before it festered. But as I looked up, my client caught my eye in the mirror, her lips pressed into a thin line, her gaze flicking between her hair and my reflection. She’d been quiet since I rinsed out the colour, and now I could see the disappointment in her face. I remembered the training: always check in, always make it right, especially with first-timers. My hands trembled slightly as I set down the comb. I could feel the weight of both expectations—Mia needed me as her friend, my client needed me as her hairdresser. I stood there, torn, the phone heavy in my pocket, the silence stretching between me and the woman in the chair.
